answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each new agent to stake a refundable deposit locked behind a reputation bridge: to cross from newcomer to trusted trader, the agent must complete verifiable work for existing members over weeks, like a slow climb up a knoll rather than a sprint. Each identity costs real compute and time, and misbehavior burns the stake - like an opal that shatters once, not twice. Attackers face linearly rising costs per fake identity while honest agents pay once.
